newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends lower on fund outflow.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends lower on fund outflow.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended lower against its U.S. counterpart on Thursday due to an increase in outflow of foreign funds triggered by a government stock sell-off plan, dealers said.

The local unit, which virtually stood still in the morning reflecting a quiet trend overseas, finished at T$27.648 against Wednesday's T$27.609 close after demand for the greenback rose in the afternoon session.
Turnover through dealers was a heavy US$351.5 million.
Taiwan's provincial government announced on Wednesday that it would speed its selldown of equity in the "big three" state-run commercial banks -- First, Hua Nan and Chang Hwa.
"The government's selloff plan scared stock investors, and a number of foreign institutional investors moved their funds out of the bourse and sent them abroad," said a foreign bank dealer.
The announcement caused Taiwan's benchmark stock index to drop 122.68 points or 1.42 percent to 8,492 on Thursday.
Dealers expected the local currency to continue its downswing in the near term.
A T$27.63-67 range was seen for Friday.
